strategist.name: The Strategist
strategist.tagline: Directs energy toward a long game others have not named yet.
strategist.description: The Strategist combines intellectual range with structured follow-through and an independent streak. You tend to frame problems as systems, look several moves ahead, and prefer a plan you can defend.
preferences: Clear goals with room to choose the method
Time to think before a high-stakes decision
strengths: Connecting a distant outcome to the next concrete step
Holding a standard when a group drifts
Saying the unfashionable true thing
growth_areas: Leaving space for people who need more warmth than a plan
Noticing when speed is being confused with quality
Inviting dissent before the strategy hardens
strategist.communication: You likely speak in conclusions, priorities, and trade-offs. Others may hear certainty even when you are still exploring.
strategist.leadership: You may lead by setting direction and expecting ownership. Coaching lands better when you also name the human cost of the plan.
strategist.relationships: Loved ones may want more of the process, not only the decision. Sharing uncertainty can feel inefficient and still be connecting.
strategist.work_environment: Best with autonomy, a real problem, and colleagues who can challenge the idea rather than the person.
reflections: Where am I optimizing a plan that no longer matches the people in it?
What would I decide if I had to explain it to someone I respect and disagree with?
exercises: Write the strategy in one paragraph, then rewrite it as a letter to a skeptic.
Ask one person what they need from you besides the plan.

visionary.name: The Visionary
visionary.tagline: Sees a future worth gathering people around.
visionary.description: The Visionary pairs imagination with social energy and interpersonal warmth. You tend to paint possibility, bring people into it, and leave some of the scaffolding for later.
preferences: Collaborators who can translate a picture into steps
strengths: Making an abstract idea feel personally relevant
Energizing a room that has gone flat
Holding hope without requiring proof first
growth_areas: Finishing the unglamorous middle of a project
Distinguishing a compelling story from a testable plan
Protecting focus when every idea is interesting
visionary.communication: You likely think out loud and use images, analogies, and invitations. Listeners may need the next action stated plainly.
visionary.leadership: You may lead by inspiration. Pair every vision with an owner, a date, and a definition of done.
visionary.relationships: You bring warmth and possibility. Partners may need you to stay with ordinary details, not only the next chapter.
visionary.work_environment: Thrives in early-stage, cross-functional, or creative work with human contact.
reflections: Which idea still deserves energy, and which is only novelty?
Who is carrying the operations I prefer not to see?
exercises: Choose one idea and write only the next three boring steps.
Ask a practical colleague to red-team the vision for 15 minutes.

innovator.name: The Innovator
innovator.tagline: Breaks a stuck pattern by trying the unofficial path.
innovator.description: The Innovator is idea-driven, socially bold, and relatively independent of group harmony. You experiment in public, challenge defaults, and move on when a method stops teaching you something.
preferences: Problems that have not been solved the same way twice
Sparse process until quality actually requires it
strengths: Generating options when a team is boxed in
Tolerating the awkwardness of a first version
Questioning sacred cows without waiting for a mandate
growth_areas: Staying through implementation after the insight
Reading the room when disruption is landing as disregard
Documenting enough that others can continue the work
innovator.communication: Direct, fast, and idea-first. You may skip the interpersonal runway other people need.
innovator.leadership: You may lead by example and challenge. People follow more readily when they know what will not change.
innovator.relationships: Excitement is easy; repetition is the work. Loved ones may experience your next project as abandonment of the last shared one.
innovator.work_environment: Startups, R&D, design, or any role where questioning the brief is allowed.
reflections: What am I leaving unfinished because the next idea is more interesting?
Where would a little more consideration cost me almost nothing?
exercises: Ship a small improvement to an existing system instead of starting a new one.
Before a critique, name one thing that is already working.

analyst.name: The Analyst
analyst.tagline: Finds the structure hiding inside a messy question.
analyst.description: The Analyst brings high openness and conscientiousness to a more reserved, independent stance. You like models, evidence, and work you can stand behind without a crowd.
preferences: Decisions that can be reconstructed later
strengths: Separating signal from noise
Building a case other people can audit
Holding complexity without rushing to a slogan
growth_areas: Sharing thinking before it feels finished
Allowing a good-enough decision when data will not arrive
Noticing the relational impact of being right
analyst.communication: Precise and compact. Others may need more context and warmth than feels necessary to you.
analyst.leadership: You may lead through quality of thought. Influence grows when you narrate the 'why' and invite a challenge early.
analyst.relationships: Loyalty often shows up as reliability and problem-solving. Partners may also want unsolved presence.
analyst.work_environment: Research, engineering, analysis, strategy, or any craft with a high error cost.
reflections: Where am I using more analysis to avoid a human conversation?
What decision is 80% clear and waiting for courage, not data?
exercises: Explain your current problem to a non-expert in five sentences.
Time-box research and decide at the alarm.

explorer.name: The Explorer
explorer.tagline: Learns by moving toward the unmarked part of the map.
explorer.description: The Explorer prefers practical freedom, lower structure, and a quieter independent path. You learn from terrain, not from a curriculum, and you resist being over-defined.
strengths: Adapting when the plan collapses
Noticing what is actually happening on the ground
Protecting personal freedom without needing an audience
growth_areas: Committing long enough for skill to compound
Letting selected people depend on you
Building just enough structure that freedom survives busy seasons
explorer.communication: Spare and experiential. You may under-explain inner life and over-index on what you did.
explorer.leadership: You may lead by scouting. Teams need a breadcrumb trail if they are going to follow.
explorer.relationships: You offer adventure and honesty. Others may need more scheduled closeness than feels natural.
explorer.work_environment: Field work, independent contracting, operations in motion, or roles with changing conditions.
reflections: Which commitment would make my freedom more meaningful, not less?
What am I calling freedom that is actually avoidance of being known?
exercises: Keep one recurring ritual for 30 days.
Tell one person the unpolished reason you want to leave or stay.

organizer.name: The Organizer
organizer.tagline: Turns care into a system people can actually use.
organizer.description: The Organizer is practical, structured, reserved, and considerate. You make life work for other people by putting pieces in place before they are missed.
preferences: Help that is useful rather than dramatic
strengths: Anticipating logistical failure
Keeping promises without requiring applause
Creating order that reduces other people's stress
growth_areas: Asking for help before resentment builds
Allowing a little mess where creativity needs it
Not treating every change as a threat to quality
organizer.communication: Concrete, sequential, and responsible. You may understate your own needs.
organizer.leadership: You may lead by making the machine run. Remember to name the purpose, not only the checklist.
organizer.relationships: You show love through reliability. Partners may still need words and play, not only a well-run household or team.
organizer.work_environment: Operations, program management, administration, healthcare logistics, education support.
reflections: What would I stop doing if I trusted other people 10% more?
Where is order serving people, and where is it serving my anxiety?
exercises: Delegate one recurring task and do not take it back for two weeks.
Schedule unstructured time and protect it like a meeting.

advocate.name: The Advocate
advocate.tagline: Stands with people who would otherwise go unheard.
advocate.description: The Advocate is warm, relatively unstructured, and more reserved than evangelical. You notice injustice or unmet need and feel responsible to respond, often one relationship at a time.
preferences: Small groups where honesty is possible
Flexibility to respond to the person in front of you
strengths: Seeing the human consequence of a policy
Staying with someone in difficulty
Speaking for fairness even when it is inconvenient
growth_areas: Boundaries so compassion does not become depletion
Choosing a few fights instead of every fight
Accepting that not everyone wants to be rescued
advocate.communication: Values-led and personal. You may assume others share the same emotional data.
advocate.leadership: You may lead from care. Pair advocacy with a sustainable plan and shared ownership.
advocate.relationships: You are loyal and attuned. Watch for over-functioning and quiet scorekeeping.
advocate.work_environment: Counseling-adjacent roles, community work, customer advocacy, people operations, mission-driven teams.
reflections: Whose need am I meeting, and whose need am I avoiding in myself?
What would 'enough' look like this week?
exercises: Practice a kind no in writing before you say it.
Name one cause you will not take on this month.

connector.name: The Connector
connector.tagline: Builds the room where the right people find each other.
connector.description: The Connector is outgoing, structured, practical, and people-centered. You remember names, contexts, and who should talk to whom, and you like making a network feel like a neighborhood.
strengths: Making strangers into a working group
Keeping relationships warm over time
Translating between very different personalities
growth_areas: Solitude that is not just recovery from over-booking
Depth with a few people, not only breadth
Saying no to one more introduction
connector.communication: Warm, fast, and inclusive. You may fill silence that someone else needed.
connector.leadership: You may lead through relationships. Document decisions so the network is not the only source of truth.
connector.relationships: You bring energy and belonging. Partners may need you to be unreachable sometimes — on purpose.
connector.work_environment: Community, sales with integrity, recruiting, partnership roles, campus or member organizations.
reflections: Who knows the real me when I am not hosting?
Which relationship am I maintaining out of habit rather than care?
exercises: Have one conversation this week with no networking agenda.
Block a half-day with notifications off.

diplomat.name: The Diplomat
diplomat.tagline: Finds a livable path between competing truths.
diplomat.description: The Diplomat combines imagination and order with a quieter, considerate presence. You can hold more than one perspective and still produce a coherent next step.
preferences: Solutions that people can live with
strengths: De-escalating without erasing the issue
Writing or speaking in a way that both sides can hear
Building process that feels fair
growth_areas: Taking a stand before everyone is comfortable
Not mediating yourself out of your own needs
Moving from consensus-seeking to time-bounded decision
diplomat.communication: Careful, qualifying, and fair-minded. Others may want a clearer recommendation.
diplomat.leadership: You may lead by facilitation. Facilitation still needs a decision and an owner.
diplomat.relationships: You keep peace. Make sure peace is not silence.
diplomat.work_environment: Policy, product, counseling, cross-functional program roles, education, stakeholder-heavy work.
reflections: What am I smoothing over that needs a name?
If I could not keep everyone happy, what would I choose?
exercises: State your preference first, then the range of options.
Let a small conflict stay unresolved for 24 hours and observe the urge to fix it.

builder.name: The Builder
builder.tagline: Makes something durable that was only a sketch yesterday.
builder.description: The Builder is practical, structured, outgoing, and independently driven. You like visible progress, real materials or real metrics, and a team that ships.
strengths: Turning a vague goal into a sequence of work
Holding the line on quality at delivery
Motivating a group through momentum
growth_areas: Listening before laying the foundation
Leaving room for ideas that do not yet have a blueprint
Resting without needing to earn it
builder.communication: Action-oriented and blunt in a useful way. Check that people felt included, not only assigned.
builder.leadership: You may lead from the front of the work. Delegation is how the building outlives you.
builder.relationships: You provide. Remember that presence is also a form of providing.
builder.work_environment: Engineering, operations, skilled trades, product delivery, entrepreneurship with a shipping culture.
reflections: What am I building to avoid feeling something?
Who did I not consult because it would have slowed the pour?
exercises: Ask for a critique of the plan before you start.
Finish 30 minutes earlier than you think you should, twice this week.

mentor.name: The Mentor
mentor.tagline: Grows other people without needing to own their success.
mentor.description: The Mentor sits at the high end of openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, and agreeableness. You like developing people, holding a standard, and staying in conversation while someone becomes more themselves.
preferences: Teaching that changes behavior, not only knowledge
Work with a human development component
strengths: Seeing potential slightly ahead of the person
Giving feedback that is both kind and specific
Building rituals of growth
growth_areas: Allowing people to fail without rescuing
Receiving mentoring, not only offering it
Keeping your own goals from being displaced by everyone else's
mentor.communication: Encouraging, structured, and narrative. Watch for over-talking when the other person needs to think.
mentor.leadership: You may lead as a coach. Coaching still requires decisions that not everyone will like.
mentor.relationships: You are generous with attention. Make sure the relationship is mutual, not a classroom.
mentor.work_environment: Education, coaching, leadership development, people management, community building.
reflections: Where am I teaching to feel needed?
What do I want to learn that I have been too busy teaching to start?
exercises: Ask someone to mentor you in a skill you are average at.
In your next 1:1, speak 30% less than usual.

investigator.name: The Investigator
investigator.tagline: Follows a question until the easy answers fall away.
investigator.description: The Investigator is intellectually curious, flexible, reserved, and independent. You disappear into a question, distrust slogans, and would rather be accurate than agreeable.
preferences: The right to change your mind in public
strengths: Noticing the exception that ruins a tidy theory
Sustained curiosity
Intellectual honesty
growth_areas: Coming back with a conclusion others can use
Relationships that are not only shared interests
Body, sleep, and ordinary life as part of the method
investigator.communication: Question-heavy and precise. People may feel quizzed rather than met.
investigator.leadership: You may lead by inquiry. Teams still need a call when the investigation could continue forever.
investigator.relationships: Intimacy may start with ideas. Practice asking how someone feels, not only what they think.
investigator.work_environment: Research, journalism, security, science, specialist consulting, any role that rewards being wrong first.
reflections: What question am I using to postpone a decision?
Who gets my warmth, not only my mind?
exercises: Write the current best answer, including what would falsify it.
Have a conversation with no follow-up questions for five minutes — only reflections.

creator.name: The Creator
creator.tagline: Gives inner life a form other people can encounter.
creator.description: The Creator is imaginative, flexible, more private, and warm. You make meaning through craft — words, images, products, environments — and you need solitude to hear yourself.
preferences: Unstructured time that is actually protected
A small audience of people who get it
Work with an aesthetic or expressive dimension
strengths: Original synthesis
Sensitivity to tone, beauty, and fit
Giving language to something others only felt
growth_areas: Sharing work before it feels ready
Money, distribution, and the unromantic half of a creative life
Not collapsing when feedback is clumsy
creator.communication: Evocative and sometimes indirect. Others may need you to say the ask plainly.
creator.leadership: You may lead by taste and example. Make criteria explicit so people are not guessing.
creator.relationships: You offer depth and atmosphere. Partners may need more ordinary updates than your inner world supplies automatically.
creator.work_environment: Design, writing, research-creation, product craft, any role with a blank page.
reflections: What would I make if no one impressive were watching?
Where am I hiding in revision?
exercises: Publish a small piece of work at 80% polish.
Ask for one piece of specific feedback and implement it.

collaborator.name: The Collaborator
collaborator.tagline: Makes the we stronger than the brightest I.
collaborator.description: The Collaborator is practical, flexible, outgoing, and cooperative. You like being in the mix, sharing credit, and solving the problem that is in the room today.
preferences: Roles where relationships are part of the job
strengths: Keeping morale and motion at the same time
Compromising without keeping a bitter ledger
Making other people better in real time
growth_areas: Holding a dissenting view when the group is rolling
Protecting individual craft from endless consensus
Not over-accommodating at your own expense
collaborator.communication: Inclusive and verbal. Silence may feel like a problem you need to fix.
collaborator.leadership: You may lead as a peer. Sometimes the group needs a captain more than another teammate.
collaborator.relationships: You are easy to live with. Practice wanting something that is only yours.
collaborator.work_environment: Cross-functional teams, customer success, ensemble performing, community operations.
reflections: What do I actually want, independent of the group?
Where did I say yes to keep the peace?
exercises: In a meeting, wait until two other people have spoken before you synthesize.
Make a personal decision this week without a poll.

independent-thinker.name: The Independent Thinker
independent-thinker.tagline: Keeps a private standard when the room wants a slogan.
independent-thinker.description: The Independent Thinker is practical, structured, reserved, and self-directed. You trust your own evaluation, dislike being managed in the small things, and would rather be consistent than popular.
preferences: Rules that make sense, not rules for their own sake
strengths: Resisting social contagion
Doing the unglamorous correct thing
Self-sufficiency
growth_areas: Letting trusted people influence you sooner
Signaling care, not only competence
Flexibility when the world refuses your outline
independent-thinker.communication: Economical. People may fill in a colder story than you intend.
independent-thinker.leadership: You may lead by example and high standards. Explain the standard; do not assume it is obvious.
independent-thinker.relationships: You offer steadiness. Warmth may need to be scheduled until it is a habit.
independent-thinker.work_environment: Specialist individual-contributor roles, quality, finance, independent practice, any job with a clear personal craft.
reflections: Where is independence actually isolation?
What would I do if I did not have to be the one who is right?
exercises: Ask for input on a decision you could make alone.
Offer an unsolicited specific appreciation.

motivator.name: The Motivator
motivator.tagline: Lights a fire under a stalled group — including yourself.
motivator.description: The Motivator is practical, flexible, outgoing, and independently forceful. You push for action, raise energy, and dislike drifting. Harmony is optional; motion is not.
preferences: Contests, launches, and moments that count
strengths: Breaking inertia
Speaking courage into a hesitant room
Recovering quickly after a miss
growth_areas: Not turning every moment into a performance
Listening for the person who cannot match your pace
Building systems so motivation is not the only fuel
motivator.communication: High volume, high certainty. Check whether people feel inspired or run over.
motivator.leadership: You may lead by rallying. Rallying without a plan becomes noise.
motivator.relationships: You bring heat and loyalty. Partners may need quiet companionship without a goal.
motivator.work_environment: Sales, athletics, campaigning, founding, turnaround work, coaching for performance.
reflections: Who have I been trying to motivate who actually needs rest?
What am I driving so I do not have to feel doubt?
exercises: Spend one hour with no agenda and no self-improvement.
Ask someone what kind of support they want before you pep-talk.
